voyage.name: Bahnhofstrasse
voyage.content: One of the busiest and best-known shopping streets in the world. Highly refined. Certainly a must-see for every tourist in Zurich!

voyage.name: Lindenhof
voyage.content: The hill in the heart of the old town. A beautiful view of the city and one time location of a Roman fort.

voyage.name: Lake Promenade
voyage.content: Especially during summer, the lake is a beautiful place to spend the evening or the weekend. Starting from Bellevue, the boardwalk goes for about three kilometers along the lake towards Tiefenbrunnen. About halfway from Bellevue there is a meadow where you will find thousands of people on a sunny day.

voyage.name: Grossmünster
voyage.content: Old Romanesque church, symbol of reformed Zurich, where reformer Huldrych Zwingli was appointed the people's priest in 1519. Go up the tower for a great view of Zurich, though the stairs can be quite small and steep.

voyage.name: Fraumünster
voyage.content: Old Gothic church (former convent) with window paintings made by Marc Chagall. No photos or videos allowed inside.

voyage.name: Schanzengraben
voyage.content: A small canal that used to be part of the city fortifications between Limmat and Sihl. From the main station, go to Gessnerallee, find the stairways down to the tiny creek, and walk all the way to the lake.

voyage.name: Langstrasse
voyage.content: Red light district of Zurich, with more drug dealers and police than usual, but interesting because even this most notorious spot in Switzerland is so clean and safe. The area is the most overtly multicultural spot of the town. Ateliers and stylish bars sit side by side the strip clubs.

voyage.name: Friedhof Fluntern
voyage.content: cemetery with lots of famous people most notably James Joyce who lived in Zurich for quite some time, the writer Elias Canetti and a few nobel prize winners are also buried there

voyage.name: Zoo
voyage.price: Fr. 26 for adults (Fr. 19 for those under 25)
voyage.content: With the new Masoala Rainforest Hall, the Zoo is really worth a visit!

voyage.name: China Garden
voyage.content: This small but beautiful Chinese garden was offered to the city of Zurich by the Chinese city of Kunming as symbol of gratitude after Zurich helped Kunming with technical knowledge. It can be very well combined with a stroll along the lake or a visit to the Pavillon Le Corbusier.

voyage.name: Niederdorf
voyage.content: The old town offers beautiful alleys, restaurants and shopping mainly aimed at younger consumers. In the evenings, people visit the Niederdorf's many bars.

voyage.name: Zurich West
voyage.content: This modern quarter used to be an industrial one, but modern urban developments made it into a centre of vibrant night life.

voyage.name: Landesmuseum
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00–17:00 and most public holidays including Mon, Thu until 19ː00
voyage.content: This is the place to go if you want to learn more about the history of Switzerland. There are permanent exhibitions on history, archaeology and art. Changing temporary exhibitions usually revolve around Swiss topics.

voyage.name: Kunsthaus
voyage.price: Fr. 16/11 for the permanent collection. Free on Wednesdays
voyage.content: Zurich's most famous art museum. The collection includes works from many Swiss artists, such as the sculptures of Alberto Giacometti or the paintings of Ferdinand Hodler. There are also major works from international artists on display. The museum is building a new extension, scheduled to open in 2020 and thus parts of the museum might be closed at any given time.

voyage.name: Johann Jacobs Museum
voyage.content: A museum that describes the complex history of global trade routes and goods and the culture around them.

voyage.name: Pavillon Le Corbusier
voyage.content: This is the last building designed by the Swiss architect le Corbusier. The Pavillon was built after his death as a museum dedicated to his work. Access to the building has long been difficult and expensive, also due to a legal fight between the former patron and initiator of the building and the city of Zurich. Now it is however managed by the city and open to the public. The highlight of the museum is of course the

voyage.name: Rietberg Museum
voyage.content: This is one of the largest art museums in Switzerland, administered by the City of Zurich. Its focus lies on the traditional and contemporary arts and cultures of Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Oceania. The complex consists of three nineteenth-century villas and a coach house, as well as a twenty-first century underground extension crowned by the Emerald, a glass pavilion that opened in 2007, designed by architects

voyage.name: Zoological Museum
voyage.content: Showcases the zoological collection of the university of Zurich. The first floor has local fauna whereas the lower floor has animals from all over the world.

voyage.name: FIFA World Football Museum
voyage.content: Explores the world of football and the FIFA.

voyage.name: Villa Patumbah
voyage.content: Stunning 19th century villa, which houses an architectural history museum (Heimatschutzzentrum).

voyage.name: Polybahn
voyage.price: Fr. 1.20, free with Zürich Card or a valid ZVV ticket for Zone 110
voyage.hours: Operates Mon-Fri 06:45–19:15, Sat 07:30–14:00, closed on Sun and public holidays
voyage.content: A 19th-century funicular, up the steep hill for a fine view. Starts at tram station Central and goes up to the ETH. Nice terrace up there. During the week, the student cafeteria below the terrace is also open to the public.

voyage.name: Oberer/Unterer Letten
voyage.content: If you go to Zurich during summer take your swimwear with you. The clean river at both the public river baths "Oberer Letten" (mainly youngsters) and "Unterer Letten" (also families) is used by the locals to cool down after hot days. Jump in upstream and the river will carry you down. Right in the middle of the town there is also a wooden floating bath for women only Frauenbad Stadthausquai at the start of the Limmat

voyage.name: trip on the Zürichsee
voyage.content: With one of the two old steam ships. There are a few different routes you can choose from, which will vary mainly in the distance. Journeys usually start from Bürkliplatz. Steam ships operate between April and mid-October.

voyage.name: Limmat river cruise
voyage.price: Fr. 4.30, free with Zürich Card or a valid ZVV ticket for Zone 110
voyage.content: Offers views of the old town and Lake Zurich. Operates between April and October.

voyage.name: Uetliberg
voyage.price: Free with Zürich Card or a valid ZVV ticket for the Zones 110, 154, and 155 (costs 4 zones). CHF 2.50 to go up the observation tower
voyage.content: A hill overlooking Zurich. You can hike up, or take a train from the "SZU" part of the main station on the S10, which takes about 20 minutes from Zurich HB. Enjoy the 360-degree view from a tall viewing tower (not for vertigo sufferers!) This is also the Start of the Planetenweg (planetary walk), a 12-km (8-mile) walk along the ridge with models of the planets along the way. These are scaled down in true proportion t

voyage.name: Street Parade
voyage.content: The biggest open air techno rave in Europe. It happens one day each year on the second Saturday of August, during which trucks which function as mobile soundsystems ("Love mobiles") start driving along the lake side, starting from the east at Utoquai and ending at the west at Hafen Enge. Every year this event attracts nearly a million visitors who dance in the streets to the music which you can hear from anywhere in

voyage.name: Swiss national day
voyage.content: 1st of August — Celebrations are carried out in many cities in the evenings and fireworks are launched at night. Watch them over the lake, or if you're experienced with safely launching fireworks yourself, you can buy them in the days leading up to the national holiday and have fun. The display over the Rheinfall, one hour away by S-Bahn, is also extremely popular.

voyage.name: Sechseläuten (Sächsilüüte)
voyage.content: On the third Monday of April, the guilds of Zurich celebrate their traditional spring festival with the burning of the snow man (Böögg). A procession of several hundreds of people with historical guild costumes and horses takes place in the centre of the town.

voyage.name: Caliente Festival
voyage.content: The largest Latin festival in Europe. Held every year in early July. Try all types of Latin American food and listen to samba, merengue & co. Huge crowds.

voyage.name: Züri Fäscht
voyage.content: A weekend festival celebrating Zurich, which occurs every 3 years (last held 7-9 July 2023). It is visited by around 2 million people. In 2023, the committee that had so far organized the Züri Fäscht cancelled their involvement with the event and the partnership with the city. Whether another organization will take over for 2026 is, as of August 2024, unknown.

voyage.name: Zürcher Theater Spektakel
voyage.hours: Last two weeks of Aug, from 17:00
voyage.content: A festival for the performing arts. Held along the lake on the Landiwiese near Rote Fabrik and features a number of free performances. Usually in August.

voyage.name: Opernhaus
voyage.content: The Zurich Opera shows frequently changing productions of world famous operas with top artists. As with the Schauspielhaus, students get a big last-minute discount. The best seats costs Fr. 45 for students.

voyage.name: Rote Fabrik
voyage.content: An old silk factory converted to a centre of youth culture and art in the 1980s. The Red Factory became one of the most exciting parts of cultural life. An artists' coop, a couple of kilometers south, form along the west bank of Lake Zurich. They have a variety of events, including music, film, and theater, including a restaurant.

voyage.name: Schauspielhaus
voyage.content: Zurich's Schauspielhaus is one of the most important theatres in the German speaking part of Europe. The Schauspielhaus has several locations, the most important one being the Pfauen. Students can get really cheap last minute tickets (10 minutes before the show) if they show their student ID. The best seats, if available, cost Fr. 20 that way.

voyage.name: Theater am Neumarkt
voyage.content: Closer to downtown.

voyage.name: Tonhalle Maag
voyage.content: During the renovation of the Tonhalle concert house the internationally renowned classical orchestra, the Tonhalle Orchester Zürich, plays at the intermediately built Tonhalle Maag concert hall. From season 2019/20, Paavo Järvi leads the orchestra.

voyage.name: Cinema Arthouse Le Paris
voyage.content: Frequently changing arthouse movies; students get a discount.

voyage.name: Bahnhofstrasse
voyage.content: Runs from the Zürich Train Main station "Hauptbahnhof" right down to the lake. Bahnhofsstrasse is famous for being one of the most exclusive and expensive shopping streets in the world. Here you can get anything from diamond rings to chocolate to fur coats. Globus and Jelmoli are two fiercely competitive department stores, both of which carry items from many high-end brands.

voyage.name: Niederdorf
voyage.content: The Old Part of Zurich which expands from "Bellevue" by the Lake right to "Central" which is just over the river from the train station. The Niederdorf is more for young people. Aside from a lot of fast food places you will find a lot of trendy clothes stores here.

voyage.name: Löwenstrasse
voyage.content: Runs west of Bahnhofstrasse from the main train station, has shops selling everyday items and a large branch of Migros, a department store chain.

voyage.name: Teuscher
voyage.content: — An upscale confiserie that specializes in truffles. There are three stores in Zürich.

voyage.name: St. Jakobs Confiserie
voyage.content: Badenerstrasse 41. The background organisation, Behindertenwerk St. Jacob, aims at providing jobs for disabled people.

voyage.name: Schweizer Heimatwerk
voyage.content: Also branches at the Bahnhofstrasse 2 and the airport. Quality Swiss handicrafts and other Swiss-made products presented in a gallery-like setting. You won't find many cuckoo clocks and the like here (cuckoo clocks are not really Swiss, they are from the Black Forest (Schwarzwald) in Germany!), the emphasis is on real traditional crafts and the work of modern craftspeople. You will find things like sleek modern hand-

voyage.name: Flohmarkt Bürkliplatz (Fleamarket)
voyage.content: Fairly relaxed yet large flea market with many interesting stalls.

voyage.name: Flohmarkt Kanzlei (Fleamarket)
voyage.content: A big flea market that hosts up to 400 stalls on busy days.

voyage.name: Orell Füssli
voyage.content: Largest bookshop in Zürich, including a large "English Bookshop" section on the third floor.

voyage.name: Sihlcity
voyage.content: A good old fashioned shopping mall, which is a 5-minute S-Bahn ride away from the main station. It comprises some 100,000 m² of rental space with a range of facilities, such as restaurants, a shopping center, a multiplex cinema, entertainment, health and fitness/wellness area, nightclub, a Four Points hotel and a chapel.

voyage.name: Rheinfelder Bierhalle
voyage.content: In this huge and boisterous restaurant you get good value food and rich portions (only try the Jumbo Jumbo Cordon-Bleu when really hungry). Cheap beer. Service can range from very good to poor depending who is working that day.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Molino
voyage.content: Pizzas and pastas in a relaxed setting. Check website for more locations.

voyage.name: Baba's take-away (Restaurant Pumpstation)
voyage.content: Part of the Restaurant Pumpstation is located direct at the lake promenade (south of Banhof Stadelhofen). From April–October, serves fresh grilled sausages, ribs, and chicken for about Fr. 6-10.
A nice Turkish place with remarkably good kebab, friendly service, and possibility to seat conveniently inside.

voyage.name: Sternen Grill
voyage.content: Zurich's most famous sausage stand near Bellevue tram stop. Red or white sausages for around Fr. 6 (Aug 2015), a piece of bread and (hot!) mustard is included.

voyage.name: Gambrinus
voyage.content: A typical Swiss restaurant with good food and cold beer. It is located in the Red Light District (Langstrasse) of Zurich and is not the ideal place to bring children or acquaintances. Gambrinus looks like a pub more than anything else, but the staff are friendly and speak English. Try the Zürigschnätzlets mit Rösti or the fondue (one of the best in town).

voyage.name: Ah-Hua
voyage.content: Offers delicious Thai dishes to budget prices. Great pit-stop in a Langstrasse pub crawl.

voyage.name: Bank
voyage.content: Restaurant, café, bar and bakery in old bank. Mostly organic and Mediterranean food.

voyage.name: Millennium Restaurant
voyage.content: Offers great pizzas, large hamburgers, spicy kebabs and other Italian and Turkish dishes at reasonable prices. Staff is very friendly and service is great. Perfect for lunch or a late-night snack.

voyage.name: Rosalys
voyage.content: Typical Swiss food including Älplermacrone (pasta with apple purée). Excellent cocktail bar, too.

voyage.name: Swiss Chuchi
voyage.content: A kitchy place serving up classic Swiss fare, mainly for tourists. Serves fondue year round.

voyage.name: Zeughauskeller
voyage.content: Offers hearty sausages, stews, rösti potato, etc., in a Brauhaus-like setting. Touristy, but good and large portions. Housed in a historical building, built in 1487.

voyage.name: Zum Kropf
voyage.content: Offers beer hall fare such as sausages and pork shanks in a somewhat refined setting. The restaurant features a beautiful painted ceiling.

voyage.name: Hiltl
voyage.content: The oldest vegetarian restaurant in Europe (from 1890).

voyage.name: Tibits
voyage.content: The fast-food outlet of Hiltl, Europe's oldest vegetarian restaurant. Offers a nice self-service buffet of fresh veggies and fruit and a surprising variety. Try the freshly squeezed juices.

voyage.name: Restaurant Eisenhof
voyage.content: Has the warm feel of an old pub. The house specialty is horse steak, served on a hot stone with fries.

voyage.name: Blinde Kuh
voyage.content: Restaurant in complete darkness, served by blind people. An amazing experience.

voyage.name: eCHo Restaurant
voyage.content: Traditional Swiss cuisine. Everything is prepared according to original recipes, and all products originate from the region.

voyage.name: Commercio
voyage.content: Excellent pasta and a busy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Commi-Halle
voyage.content: Italian food served late.

voyage.name: Globus Bellevue
voyage.content: This relatively new branch of the Globus department store in the Bellevue near the Stadelhofen station is totally dedicated to food. There is a large eatery on the ground floor that serves various fusion-type foods (decent noodle bowl) and a passable sushi bar. The ground floor has a gourmet food market, and upstairs there are kitchen wares.

voyage.name: Sprüngli Paradeplatz
voyage.content: The flagship store of the Sprüngli confectionery store chain has a beautiful turn-of-the-century style dining room upstairs that is extremely popular for breakfast, lunch and afternoon tea. Choose from the menu or from the gorgeous display case filled with beautiful cakes, tarts, open-face and regular sandwiches. Try the muesli! Great people watching too, since this is the place for an after-shopping snack for the ri

voyage.name: Masala
voyage.content: Tasty Indian cuisine.

voyage.name: Outback Lodge
voyage.content: Unrelated to the U.S. Outback Steakhouse chain. Enjoy Aussie tucker like ostrich, kangaroo, and crocodile, as well as more conventional fare. Popular with locals as well as expats. Has a hopping bar scene (see Drink section). There's also a branch in Winterthur.

voyage.name: Iroquois
voyage.content: Tex-Mex food in the trendiest part of town, with the best margaritas in Zurich.

voyage.name: Tiffin's
voyage.content: Great place for Asian food. Crowded.

voyage.name: Lily's
voyage.content: Great Thai and other Asian food. The curries are particularly good and come in huge portions. Come before 19:00 or after 21:00 if you don't want to wait.

voyage.name: Manzoni Bar
voyage.content: Authentic Italian coffee and aperitif bar that offers clients over 20 different coffee specialties and a vast take away menu. The concept was created by the Manz brothers together with Francesco Illy, the most famous coffee brand in Italy.

voyage.name: Nooba
voyage.content: Pan-Asian noodle bar, a short walk up the hill from Stadelhofen station. Stylish setting, attentive and multilingual service and a broad selection of freshly prepared noodle, rice and curry dishes.

voyage.name: Nooch
voyage.content: Yet another Pan-Asian noodle, rice and curry joint. Also has a sushi bar.

voyage.name: Ristorante Toscano
voyage.content: A very good Italian restaurant in the old part of the city (Niederdorf). You should try the Spaghetti al Bacio!

voyage.name: Bebek
voyage.content: Breakfast until 16:00. Meze dishes and bar in the evening.

voyage.name: White Elephant
voyage.content: Original Thai Food. Since 1991 it offers an authentic cuisine with the full scope of original spices.

voyage.name: Mesa Restaurant
voyage.content: Traditional kitchen with Catalan influences as one of the best restaurants in Zurich

voyage.name: Kronenhalle
voyage.content: The city's most famous restaurant where all the glitterati go to see and be seen. Good Swiss food and heavenly chocolate mousse are one reason to go, the opportunity to dine among original artwork by famous Swiss and European artists (who paid in paintings instead of money) the other.

voyage.name: Widder Hotel
voyage.content: High-class food in a cool setting. The hotel has a trendy bar, great piano music, cool red leather decor, and halogen lighting.

voyage.name: Zunfthaus Zur Waag
voyage.content: Very authentic Swiss high-end restaurant. To ensure your meal does not get cold, they split your order into 2 plates and bring you one at a time.

voyage.name: Le Dezaley
voyage.content: Traditional French-Swiss food from the French-speaking Kanton Waadt (Vaud). One of many fondue restaurants in Zurich.

voyage.name: Blaue Ente
voyage.content: Romantic cuisine in a beautiful building.

voyage.name: Coco Grill & Bar
voyage.content: Grill restaurant that offers set menus for lunch and a menu surprise for dinner (either fish or meat). Also has a good wine selection and very nice in the summer due to a small garden

voyage.name: Da Angela
voyage.content: Authentic Italian food.

voyage.name: Bar & Lounge 42
voyage.content: New York in the middle of Zurich. Exclusive whiskey, unique cocktails, premium liquors, snacks, a homemade gin and an elegant smoker's lounge with a broad selection of cigars.

voyage.name: Bierhalle Wolf
voyage.content: A lively beer hall often with live music. In addition to the beer selection, they serve great local food.

voyage.name: Edi's Weinstube
voyage.content: nice wine bar in Niederdorf where you can get the cheapest okay wine in Zurich

voyage.name: Federal
voyage.content: A big brasserie-like bar inside the Main Station with a choice of 100 Swiss beers.

voyage.name: Nachtflug
voyage.content: Stylish, coffee and some snacks during the day, large choice of drinks at night.

voyage.name: James Joyce bar
voyage.content: Where the writer used to drink. Now mostly frequented by bankers.

voyage.name: Oliver Twist
voyage.content: An Irish/British pub with a good atmosphere, and many English-speaking foreigners. Has English ales on draught.

voyage.name: Öpfelchammer
voyage.content: Not a real pub or café, they only serve wine or water. But if you succeed in climbing over the roof beams, you get a free glass of wine to drink hanging upside down and you can mark your name into the wood afterwards.

voyage.name: Widder Garage
voyage.content: By far the best stocked whiskey bar in town, with a separate whiskey menu containing 250 single malts. In the famous hotel of the same name.

voyage.name: Corazón
voyage.content: A Spanish-themed bar with a good selection of wines and excellent service.

voyage.name: Bohemia
voyage.content: Trendy place popular for its coffee during the day and an even better nightlife. Usually a popular place for college students.

voyage.name: Barfussbar
voyage.content: During the day this is a public bath for women only. But at night (after 20:00) men are also allowed. It is a beautiful place to spend a warm summer night with a great view of Zurich.

voyage.name: Rimini
voyage.hours: Sun-Fri 19:30–00:00, Sat 17:00–00:00, only in summer and only when it's not raining
voyage.content: Another open air bar. This one is at the men's public baths. Really cool atmosphere because of the nice colored lights and the straw mats and pillows.

voyage.name: El Lokal
voyage.content: Bar, restaurant, and intimate gig venue attracting alternative crowd, "soccer vs elvis vs che guevara" themed.

voyage.name: Shamrock Irish Pub
voyage.content: Irish pub with regular events & good crowd (food served).

voyage.name: Xenix
voyage.content: Small art house cinema with a busy beer garden in summer. There's a mixture of students, bohemians, and bicycle messengers posing with their fixies.

voyage.name: Total Bar
voyage.content: Tiny bar serving a range of Zurich's microbrews. There's always good music.

voyage.name: Kasheme
voyage.content: This bar is all about good music. It features sometimes world famous DJs doing small mostly vinyl only sessions of funk, soul, disco and of course electronic music.

voyage.name: Kanonaegass Bar
voyage.content: Nice bar off Langstrasse with good drinks and good music. Bar is owned by 1990s electronic-music/trip-hop pioneer Richard Dorfmeister from Kruder & Dorfmeister.

voyage.name: Mars Bar
voyage.content: Bar frequented mostly by the leftist youth of Zurich.

voyage.name: Acid
voyage.content: Hip café and bar.

voyage.name: Gotthard Bar
voyage.content: This dive bar exists since forever. It's almost always packed, there's live music sometimes. Very mixed crowd but very likeable place.

voyage.name: 4. Akt
voyage.content: Teens and tweens love this place.

voyage.name: Vineria Centrale
voyage.content: A cool low key Italian wine bar. Go there for aperitivo and good times.

voyage.name: Frau Gerolds Garten
voyage.content: huge open air bar with urban gardening and little shops inside. great during summer but also offers a couple tables inside during winter

voyage.name: Aya Bar
voyage.content: A roof lounge on top the Cinemax complex. Older crowd, very expensive, but stylish.

voyage.name: Moods
voyage.content: Jazz club in the Schiffbau complex, concerts on Saturdays.

voyage.name: X-Tra
voyage.content: Big club with events and concerts, the famously have a weekly goth (dark scene) party. Can be trashy depending on the party, check beforehand

voyage.name: Hive Club
voyage.content: Many rooms to wander through and listen to DJs from Switzerland and abroad. Sometimes offers nonstop parties during the weekends. Focus on Techno and House.

voyage.name: Helsinki
voyage.content: Small bar and club with nice atmosphere, especially in summer when the outdoor area is open. Live concerts most nights and safe haven for independent artists from all over Switzerland.

voyage.name: Gonzo
voyage.content: A basement club that generally plays no electronic music. Can be lots of fun but the queues are long and the door can be strict. Great on Wednesday (Hip-Hop) and Thursdays (students).

voyage.name: Klaus
voyage.content: Member only club that is mostly frequented by the local "scene". Features mostly local DJs but is the new place to be. Befriend a local to get in.

voyage.name: Kauz
voyage.content: Underground club with great drinks and cocktail selection. house techno and other electronic music

voyage.name: Exil
voyage.content: small club and concert venue in Kreis 5. Look up what's happening beforehand. Music can range from trap/hiphop to indie rock

voyage.name: Friedas Büxe
voyage.content: small underground club with techno and house music, beloved by the local scene

voyage.name: Rathauscafé
voyage.content: Coffee and a croissant in the morning, moving over to sparkling wine in the afternoon and early evening. Nice terrace in the summer. Mixed crowd, friendly service.

voyage.name: Cranberry
voyage.content: Very crowded on Fridays and Saturdays 20:00–00:00, before the boys head to the clubs.

voyage.name: Barfüsser
voyage.content: Once Europe's oldest gay bar, it has now been converted into a fancy and large lounge and sushi place. Has a relaxed atmosphere and mixed crowd.

voyage.name: Heldenbar
voyage.content: Heldenbar is the weekly get together of the local LGBTQI scene.

voyage.name: Couchsurfing
voyage.content: Has a lot of members in Zurich. Public transport is very fast and good, so also consider staying in surrounding areas instead of in the city centre. Remember that couchsurfing is about the community and not only a free place to crash.

voyage.name: Youth hostel
voyage.price: From Fr. 42 for a dormitory bed with breakfast; Fr. 104 for a single room with shower
voyage.content: A little way out of the centre, but the city is easily reached by public transport (take the S-Bahn to Wollishofen and walk over the hill). A clean and sleek facility, if a little quiet.

voyage.name: Hotel Marta
voyage.content: A "clean and friendly" place which doubles as a hostel and a one-star hotel. They also have weekly and monthly rates for rooms, and a couple of studio apartments.

voyage.name: Otter
voyage.content: A good hotel for the price. The rooms have been decorated with the kind of care that one normally expects in a much more expensive hotel, each with its own theme. You can choose from the jungle room with its hammock, or the pink Carmen, or go for the top floor apartment. Each floor's three rooms share a bath, shower and toilet (WC), with the exception of the apartment which has its own shower. Fr. 115 for a single ro

voyage.name: Hotel Splendid
voyage.content: This hotel is relatively cheap. The rooms are clean but spare. Private showers and bathrooms are not available, you share with your floor. What is really great is the location, right close to the Gemüsebrücke and the city centre. Fr. 62-85 for a single, from Fr. 160 for a 4-person room, plus Fr. 2.50 City-Taxe per person.

voyage.name: Etap Hotel
voyage.price: 90 Fr (low season) to Fr. 115 (high season) for a single room, and from Fr. 100 for double/triple occupancy. For Zurich, this is cheap
voyage.content: This hotel is in a great place if you want to party, next to some great bars and restaurants. The rooms are clean and comfortable. It's also near a tram station, which takes 10 minutes to get to the main train station.

voyage.name: Hotel Schäfli
voyage.content: The location is the draw in this somewhat run-down hotel. Situated in the old town near the station and by the charming Niederdorfstrasse, where there are tons of bars and restaurants. The shower has a timer. Be sure to get all the coins for the shower you need by Saturday, as the reception desk closes on Sundays. Fr. 102 for a double room.

voyage.name: Hotel Neufeld
voyage.content: The comfortable, modern 3-star owner-run hotel is located just a few minutes away from the city centre. All 40 new renovated rooms are comfortable and modern furnished. Perfect for businespeople and tourists. The rates start from Fr. 110 for a single and Fr. 155 for a double room, including tax breakfast and free wifi.

voyage.name: Hotel St. Georges
voyage.content: Traditional and charming owner run hotel in the city centre, 10 minutes walking distance to the train station. Convenient for businespeople as well as tourists and backpackers. The rates start from Fr. 99 for a single and Fr. 228 for a double room, including tax, breakfast and free Wifi.

voyage.name: Hotel Adler
voyage.content: Clean rooms and breakfast is included in the price. They have a terrific restaurant attached and associated with the hotel that has delicious fondue. The hotel is in a great area for foot exploration. With many bars, restaurants, and cafes all within a few minutes. They have a single computer on the second floor with free internet access.

voyage.name: Ambassador à l'Opéra
voyage.content: Four-star boutique hotel situated in the town centre, opposite the Opera House and only 10 min away from the main station Hauptbahnhof and 30 minutes from the Zurich airport. Renovated and exquisitely decorated. Single room from Fr. 220, two-person room from Fr. 390 in the low season.

voyage.name: Helmhaus
voyage.content: Three tram stops with tram number 4 from the main station. Located directly next to the Limmat in the old town of Zurich. Very traditional four star hotel with first-class service, style and modern comfort. Single room from Fr. 230, double room from Fr. 300.

voyage.name: Sorell Hotel Rex
voyage.price: Single room from Fr. 140, twin room from Fr. 190
voyage.content: Three-star hotel, 5 minutes by tram number 7 from the Hauptbahnhof. All rooms are non-smoking.

voyage.name: Wellenberg
voyage.content: The four-star Art Deco Hotel Wellenberg with its idyllic inner court terrace is in the car-free old town of Zurich, 10 walking minutes from the Hauptbahnhof. The rooms are modern and elegant. One-person room from Fr. 290, two-person room from Fr. 370.

voyage.name: Palais Kraft
voyage.content: Three luxury rooms in Zurich's most prestigious residential building. Located 2km from the centre, above the university district at Toblerplatz (Trams 5 and 6, direction Zoo), in the heart of Zurich's prime residential area. The rooms come with a large well-stocked fridge, kitchenette, 32" or bigger flat screen TV, wireless internet access, and open to the terrace of the Palais Kraft. Beginning at Fr. 385 per room/ni

voyage.name: Designer Hotel Greulich
voyage.content: Located in the heart of Zurich's vibrant Aussersihl district, the stunning Hotel Greulich is a haven of style and comfort with a renowned gourmet restaurant. Online booking.

voyage.name: Hotel St. Gotthard Zürich
voyage.content: Business hotel. A five-floor building, with 143 spacious rooms, 11 of which aresSuites, comfortable lobby and three restaurants, the Hotel Gotthard meets all the expectations of the demanding traveller. The Hotel Gotthard lies center of the city, located on the Bahnhofstrasse, within 10 minutes walk from sightseeing, the business district and Lake Zurich.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Zürich
voyage.price: €150-300 per night depending on the room type and the season
voyage.content: Clean rooms and breakfast included in most of the rates. It has a fitness centre, a bar and a restaurant. It is about 200 m away from Albisreiden Tram station (tram number 3).

voyage.name: Dorint Airport-Hotel Zürich
voyage.content: The hotel (opened in 2014) is located near the airport and offers 235 rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Widder
voyage.price: From Fr. 600 single room to Fr. 1500 for 1-bedroom suite
voyage.content: Known for excellent service and location in the old town, 1-2 min from Bahnhofstrasse.

voyage.name: Movenpick Zurich Airport Hotel
voyage.content: Glattbrugg. 5-star hotel minutes from Zurich Airport offering accommodation, 3 restaurants, meeting & conference facilities and a gym.

voyage.name: Hotel zum Storchen
voyage.content: On the river Limmat with an exclusive restaurant.

voyage.name: Baur au lac
voyage.content: Located at the lake, excellent restaurant, popular with actors, celebrities, and politicians.

voyage.name: Savoy Baur en Ville
voyage.content: Rooms are clean and modern but small.

voyage.name: Park Hyatt Zurich
voyage.content: expensive but has a very nice room and spa there is a casino too.

voyage.name: Dolder Grand
voyage.content: Kurhausstrasse 65, flagship hotel of Zurich with amazing view and excellent spa.

voyage.name: ALDEN Hotel Splügenschloss
voyage.content: A small and intimate five-star boutique hotel in Zürich, located on a quiet side street, near the lakeshore and Bahnhofstrasse. The hotel comprises of two restored landmark buildings and has a modern interior.

voyage.name: Zurich Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: International business hotel with spacious guest rooms, popular restaurants, meeting facilities and a fitness center.

voyage.name: Fischer's Fritz Camping
voyage.content: This camp site is the closest to the city. Many guests were not too happy with the facilities and the friendliness of the owners.
